meta.triageRationale: One cohesive story under a single design: the daemon side extends the existing feedback record, reject function and user lookup; the plugin side reworks one pane and adds one path to the chat host. Design choices remain (inline anchor and re-finding it after a revision, the sandboxed HTML viewer under the CSP, a decision message waiting for a running chat turn).

findings.premise: Each upstream acceptance criterion (ac1..ac8) and stakeholder decision is designed, and no non-goal is built.
findings.evidence: The Story is standalone (meta.standalone true, no DEF/HLD). I searched .insrc/artifacts/LLD-8d4b90c9ab301e66-S001.json for the criteria text: it holds only `acceptanceMapping` with ids ac1..ac8 (lines 623-677), no criterion statements and no nonGoals/specHash. The only statement of intent is citation c27 (chat decisions, 2026-10-13); each decision it names (VS Code theme only, round icon-only buttons, decision + new comments sent to chat, decision alone when no comments, artifact JSON holds the comments, wait for a running turn, open a closed chat) has a matching part in sections 2.4-2.7. The wording of ac1..ac8 itself could not be read anywhere, so one-to-one coverage is unconfirmed.
findings.action: Record the text of ac1..ac8 (or the seven requirements of c27) in the LLD so the mapping in section 6 can be checked against statements, not ids.

findings.premise: The chosen alternative (8.1 a1) describes the design that section 2 specifies.
findings.evidence: 8.1 says the daemon 'appends every comment in one write ... and only then calls the existing approve or reject function', adds 'A second new IPC workflow.companionContent', an anchor of '{ quote, sectionSlug?, blockText? }', a view gaining three fields, and a result '{ decision, recorded, entries, approved?, skipped?, rejectedAt? }'. Section 2.4 says the opposite order ('the decision first, the comments second', postcondition 'A comment is never saved with a decision that did not take effect'), has no companionContent IPC (HTML is shown through companionUri in an iframe), an anchor of { quote, sectionSlug, prefix, suffix }, five view fields, and a different result shape. [files: .insrc/artifacts/LLD-8d4b90c9ab301e66-S001.json]
findings.action: Rewrite 8.1 to match sections 2.3-2.6 and 3.1 (decision first, no workflow.companionContent, prefix/suffix anchor, the ReviewDecisionResult shape), so a builder reading the chosen option does not implement the comments-first order.

findings.premise: Today the pane approves through workflow.approve, sends request-changes through workflow.resolveComment with an empty anchor for DEF/HLD/LLD only, and reject exists only as a function the CLI calls.
findings.evidence: vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts:118-136: approve() -> 'workflow.approve'; comment() -> 'workflow.resolveComment' with `comments: [{ id: `c-${Date.now()}`, anchor: {}, body: note }]`. docs-review-panel.ts:28 `COMMENTABLE_KINDS = new Set(['DEF', 'HLD', 'LLD'])`, :1465 comment in decide: 'there is no daemon reject IPC'. The only non-test caller of rejectArtifactByJsonPath is src/cli/services/workflow.ts:174. The shell (docs-review-panel.ts:1749-1770) lays list, body, textarea and actions in page flow under renderTerminalStyle, and open() posts { type: 'theme' } (:1828).

findings.premise: appendFeedback is append-only, touches only body.feedback, does not re-render the .md, and the review view does not return feedback today.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/artifacts/provenance/writer.ts:117-150: validates author/comment, reads once, writes `{ ...artifact, body: { ...artifact.body, feedback: [...existing, entry] } }` through writeArtifactJson; no markdown write. It copies only id/author/timestamp/target/comment/kind, so the new fields do need the writer change the design lists. src/workflow/artifact-content.ts:205-213 returns artifactId, kind, renderedMarkdown, openQuestions, approvable, blockReason and the five structured records; no feedback, docPath, contentVersion, reviewer or state.

findings.premise: A message typed in the chat supersedes a running turn, and the chat host accepts messages only from its own webview.
findings.evidence: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts:124-135: ChatPanelHost is { open, adopt, dispose } only. :1272-1278 'Single-in-flight per panel: the newest message wins'; turn-lifecycle.ts:221-227 start() aborts a waiting turn and bumps the generation. submitTurn (:1288-1312) calls supersedeQueuedApprovals() then runTurn. extension.ts:566 and :668 build the two hosts separately with no reference between them.

findings.premise: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/header.ts has a user lookup (git user.name, else OS login, else 'unknown') that can be exported and gives the reviewer's name and source.
findings.evidence: There is no lookup function. header.ts:127-141 has two private helpers, defaultGitUserName(repoPath) and defaultOsUserName(); the three-step fallback is written inline inside resolveCompanionHeader (:87-89): `user: nonEmpty((deps.gitUserName ?? defaultGitUserName)(input.repoPath)) ?? nonEmpty((deps.osUserName ?? defaultOsUserName)()) ?? 'unknown'`. It yields a name only; nothing reports which step answered, which the design's reviewer.source ('git' | 'os' | 'unknown') needs. The git call returns the raw output with its newline; trimming is done by the private nonEmpty. [files: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/header.ts]
findings.action: State that a new function is extracted (for example resolveReviewer(repoPath, deps?) returning { name, source }), that resolveCompanionHeader calls it so the two cannot drift, and list header.ts as a change site with a test that the companion header's user is unchanged.

findings.premise: approveWorkflowTarget and rejectArtifactByJsonPath exist with the shapes the decision core relies on (skipped[] for a withheld approval, a reason-taking reject), and the bugfix follow-on can be reused.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/gates.ts:826-901: approveWorkflowTarget({ repoPath, artifactPath }) resolves jsonPathForMd, returns { approved, skipped, codeReview }, routing ReviewBlockedError and a blocked code-review gate into skipped[] with a reason. gates.ts:971-990: rejectArtifactByJsonPath(jsonPath, reason) throws on a blank reason (the design supplies a default) and does `delete nextMeta.approvedAt` without checking state, so the design's own pending pre-check is needed and is stated. The follow-on (src/daemon/index.ts:662-671, advanceApprovedBugfixes) needs daemonInferencePorts(db, ...) from the daemon, which fits the design's 'injected approve' function; src/workflow/review-decision.ts cannot call it directly.
findings.action: In 2.4, say explicitly that the approve function injected by src/daemon/index.ts wraps approveWorkflowTarget plus advanceApprovedBugfixes, since the follow-on is DB-bound and lives in the handler today.

findings.premise: submitExternal can open a closed chat panel and run the message at once, answering 'sent'.
findings.evidence: open() (chat-panel.ts:1655-1662) only creates and wires the channel. The session is created later, in postInitialState, which runs when the webview posts 'ready' (:1358-1363, :631 `if (session === undefined) session = deps.store.draft(available[0]!)`). The typed-message path the design reuses drops the message when there is no session: submitTurn :1289 `if (session === undefined) return;` and runTurn :1129 `if ((typed === '' && files.length === 0) || session === undefined) return;`. So on a panel that was closed, 'run at once through the same path a typed message takes' silently discards the message while submitExternal answers 'sent' and the pane reports the chat message as sent. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]
findings.action: Specify that a message submitted before the webview's 'ready' is put on the waiting list and run from postInitialState once the session exists (answer 'queued'), and add a test: submitExternal on a never-opened host delivers the message after 'ready'.

findings.premise: A queued external message is run 'when that turn reaches its end, errors or is stopped', and never collides with another turn.
findings.evidence: Three exits are not covered. (1) A turn superseded by a typed message gets no terminal callback: turn-lifecycle.ts:222-227 'the generation bump stops the previous loop reporting', and the test at turn-lifecycle.test.ts:219 asserts 'the dropped turn is told nothing more'; a message waiting behind that turn is never released unless it re-attaches to the newer turn. (2) The lifecycle exposes no 'running or waiting' state, only `live`, 'once its first event arrived' (turn-lifecycle.ts:87-88), and a turn followed after a reload (followLiveTurn, chat-panel.ts:595-620) ends through onEnd, not onTerminal. (3) onTerminal itself starts a turn: chat-panel.ts:1247-1248 calls runCompletedBatch(), which does `void runTurn(prompt, approvals.grantChain(), { suppressEcho: true })` (:550); a queued message run at the same end supersedes that approval follow-up, or is superseded by it. A chat switch (invalidate/detach) while a message waits is also unstated beyond 'in the session that is active then'. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/turn-lifecycle.ts]
findings.action: Define the host's own in-flight flag (set in runTurn and followLiveTurn, cleared on onTerminal, onError, onEnd, stop and detach), say that a superseding typed turn inherits the waiting list, and order the drain after runCompletedBatch's follow-up (the follow-up counts as a running turn). Add tests for a superseded turn and for a turn that ends with an approved batch.

findings.premise: The host can call client.decide (and re-read the document) for an artifact that is not in the pending list: a read-only open, or a document just approved or rejected.
findings.evidence: The client resolves ids only from the pending list: docs-review-client.ts:76-77 `resolvePath = (idOrPath) => mdPathById.get(idOrPath) ?? idOrPath`, and pending() does `mdPathById.clear()` then refills with pending artifacts only (:85-88). After an approve or reject the host 're-reads the pending list and the document', so the id no longer resolves and the bare artifact id is sent as mdPath, which the daemon refuses ('mdPath must resolve under docs/'). The same hits the design's stated recovery ('pressing send feedback sends them again, which is allowed in any state') and 'a read-only open ... offers send feedback'. The host today also drops any decision for a non-pending id: docs-review-panel.ts:1799 `if (!pending.has(msg.artifactId)) { ... void refreshPending(); return; }`, and a read-only open is given its path only once, as openDoc's `opts.path` (:1299). [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-panel.ts]
findings.action: State that the host keeps the docPath of the open document (from the view's new docPath) and passes that path to decide() and to the re-read, and that the pending.has guard applies to approve and reject only. Add host tests: feedback on a read-only open, and the re-read after an approve.

findings.premise: The five design finalizers can put priorFeedback 'of the artifact they are about to replace' into the new body, for DEF, HLD, LLD and PLAN.
findings.evidence: For HLD, LLD and PLAN the id comes from params (epicHash, storyId), so a re-run writes the same path and the carry-forward is workable; the finalizers are pure (they return renderedJson; the write is in synthesize.ts:82-83 and workflow-rpc.ts:334), so they must compute the path themselves with the *ArtifactPaths helpers imported at orchestrator.ts:116. For DEF it does not work: finalizeDefine mints the identity from the run, orchestrator.ts:1190 `const epicHash = computeEpicHash(runId);` and hash.ts:36-40 hashes the run id, so a re-authored Define is a new DEF-<hash>.json and there is no artifact 'about to be replaced' to read. The integration test passes only because its fixture is placed 'at the path the finalizer writes'. finalizeDefineExtend (orchestrator.ts:1255), which does rewrite an existing Define, is not in the list of five. [files: src/workflow/orchestrator.ts, src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/synthesize.ts, src/workflow/hash.ts]
findings.action: Either drop DEF from the carry-forward claim and its test, or say how a re-authored Define finds its predecessor. Say whether finalizeDefineExtend preserves body.feedback when it rewrites the Define, and name the path helper each finalizer uses to locate the prior JSON.

findings.premise: The three new FeedbackEntry fields are optional, older entries stay valid and render byte-identically, and the schema change is needed and is listed.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/artifacts/provenance/types.ts:37-42: FeedbackEntry has id, target, comment, kind? plus author/timestamp; adding optional fields breaks no reader. schema.ts:23-55: the item schema has `additionalProperties: false` with only id/author/timestamp/comment/kind/target, so anchor/decision/batchId would be rejected until schema.ts changes, which 3.1 lists. bindings.ts:81-88 renders `- **author** (timestamp) `kind` — `file`: comment`; adding the decision and quote only when present keeps old lines identical. tool.ts:85-107 coerceRequest drops unknown keys, so it also needs the listed change. src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts:206 also calls feedbackBodyLines; it needs no edit but is a render site missing from the inventory.
findings.action: Add src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts to the list of sites that render feedback, so the BUILD record is covered by the byte-identical test.

findings.premise: The five additive fields on ArtifactReviewView leave the JetBrains plugin's reader unaffected.
findings.evidence: The TypeScript side is additive (artifact-content.ts:50-78 already carries optional additive fields under the same rule). On the Kotlin side I found the DTO (jetbrains-plugin/.../daemon/DaemonGateway.kt:73 `data class ArtifactReviewViewDto(`) but a search of that file for Gson, ObjectMapper, `Json {`, ignoreUnknownKeys and FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES found nothing, so I could not confirm how the reply is deserialized or that unknown keys are ignored.
findings.action: Check the artifactContent parser in DaemonGateway.kt (near line 1525) for unknown-key tolerance and cite it in the invariant, or add a Kotlin test with the five new keys in the reply.

findings.premise: An HTML companion that cannot be shown is detectable: companionUri absent or undefined, or the frame's load event not arriving within five seconds.
findings.evidence: The shell's CSP today is `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'nonce-${nonce}';` (docs-review-panel.ts:1611), so the frame-src addition is required and is designed. The panel is created with `{ enableScripts: true }` only (extension.ts:671), so the local resource roots are VS Code's defaults. Whether a sandboxed iframe can load a webview resource address at all was not run (the design's own open question 1), and I could not run it either. The detection is doubtful on its own terms: a frame that is refused or fails to fetch usually still fires load on an error document, so 'no load within five seconds' may never trigger and the tab would show a blank frame.
findings.action: Run the probe before the build starts, as the open question recommends. If the frame is kept, detect failure by something the companion page reports (not possible under sandbox 'allow-scripts' without a message handshake) or fall back to the path line by default; state which.

findings.premise: Each acceptance criterion maps to at least one named test, in the stated framework and locations.
findings.evidence: The LLD JSON's acceptanceMapping (lines 623-677) has entries for ac1 through ac8, each with one or more proving tests that also appear in the test levels of section 6. The stated homes exist: vscode-plugin/src/chat/__tests__/docs-review-panel.test.ts, docs-review-client.test.ts, chat-panel.test.ts and chat-shell.test.ts. The pane tests use hand-built DOM stubs (docs-review-panel.test.ts:794 `createElement: (t: string) => bodyStub(t)`); a search of the test folder for getSelection/createRange found none, so the selection and range fake is new work, as the fixture line says. ac2 (theme) and part of ac8 rest on by-hand smoke checks.
findings.action: Add tests for the cases the change-site findings raise: submitExternal before the webview is ready, a message waiting behind a superseded turn, a decision on a non-pending document, and re-authoring a Define.

summary.prose: The document review pane in VS Code is rebuilt around a comment panel that stays at the bottom while the document scrolls: a rounded box with a comment field and three round icon buttons for send feedback, reject and approve, in the VS Code theme's own colours. A reviewer can select text in a markdown document and comment on it; comments are drafts until one of the three buttons is pressed, which saves them all with the decision in one step, under the reviewer's git name and the time, in the artifact's own feedback list. Earlier comments stay with the document, are shown as margin markers that open on click, oldest first, and survive a revision; HTML documents that belong to an artifact open as the page itself. The decision and the new comments are also sent to the chat as a message, so the assistant can revise or move on.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Rework the document review pane: fixed decision bar, saved inline comments, decision sent to the chat

api.name: appendFeedback
api.signature: appendFeedback(req: AppendFeedbackRequest): AppendFeedbackResult  // unchanged. New beside it in src/workflow/artifacts/provenance/writer.ts: appendFeedbackBatch(req: { artifactPath: string; entries: readonly (Omit<FeedbackEntry, 'id' | 'timestamp'>)[] }): { artifactPath: string; entryIds: string[]; total: number }  and  priorFeedback(jsonPath: string): FeedbackEntry[]

parameters.name: req.artifactPath
parameters.purpose: The artifact JSON to append to; guarded under the artifact root as today.

parameters.name: req.entries
parameters.purpose: The entries of one decision, in the order the reviewer made them. Each has author, target and comment, and may carry kind, anchor, decision and batchId.

returns.type: { artifactPath: string; entryIds: string[]; total: number }
returns.meaning: appendFeedbackBatch validates every entry first (non-empty author and comment, as appendFeedback does), then reads the artifact once, gives each entry an id and the same timestamp, pushes them all onto body.feedback and writes the JSON once. Either all entries are written or none. priorFeedback returns body.feedback of the JSON at that path, or [] when the file is missing, unreadable or has none. The design finalizers in src/workflow/orchestrator.ts (finalizeDefine, finalizeDesignEpic, finalizeDesignStory, finalizeStandaloneLld, finalizePlan) put priorFeedback of the artifact they are about to replace into the new body before they render it, so a re-authored document keeps its comments.

errors.condition: The path is outside the artifact root, the JSON is missing or malformed, the list is empty, or any entry has a blank author or comment; nothing is written.

preconditions: The artifact JSON exists under .insrc/artifacts or docs/
postconditions: No key of the artifact other than body.feedback changes, and no existing entry is edited or removed
The .md is not re-rendered by an append, as today
A document re-authored through the workflow keeps every earlier feedback entry, in order
appendFeedback and the 'artifact.feedback.append' IPC behave as before

api.name: feedbackBodyLines

returns.meaning: One bullet per entry as today. An entry with a decision shows it after the kind; an entry with an anchor shows the quoted text (cut to 120 characters) before the comment. An entry with neither renders exactly as today.

postconditions: Existing artifacts with feedback render byte-identically
No feedback still gives no section

api.name: handleArtifactContent
api.signature: handleArtifactContent(params: { repo?: string; mdPath?: string } | undefined, repoEnv: string | undefined): ArtifactReviewView | ArtifactContentError  // ArtifactReviewView gains: docPath: string; contentVersion: string; feedback?: readonly FeedbackEntry[]; reviewer: { name: string; source: 'git' | 'os' | 'unknown' }; state: 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected'

parameters.name: params.mdPath
parameters.purpose: The artifact's .md under docs/, as today.

parameters.name: params.repo
parameters.purpose: The repository; falls back to the daemon's repo as today.

returns.meaning: The view as today plus five additive fields. docPath is the .md's repo-relative path. contentVersion is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the markdown text returned. feedback is body.feedback as stored (absent when there is none). reviewer is the name comments would be saved under: git config user.name in the repo, else the OS login, else 'unknown', from the lookup in src/workflow/artifacts/companion/header.ts, which is exported for this. state is read from meta.approvedAt and meta.rejectedAt.

errors.condition: As today: repo or mdPath missing, the path outside docs/, not a .md, unreadable, or its JSON unreadable.

postconditions: Every existing field keeps its name, type and meaning, so the JetBrains plugin's reader is unaffected
The feedback list is forwarded as stored: no entry is dropped, reordered or reshaped

api.name: workflow.approve
api.signature: 'workflow.approve' is unchanged. New in the same handler map of src/daemon/index.ts: 'workflow.reviewDecision': (params: { repo?: string; mdPath: string; decision: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'feedback'; comments?: readonly ReviewDecisionComment[] }) => ReviewDecisionResult | { error: string }, delegating to handleReviewDecision in the new src/workflow/review-decision.ts.  ReviewDecisionComment = { comment: string; file?: string; version?: string; anchor?: FeedbackAnchor }.  ReviewDecisionResult = { artifactId: string; decision: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'feedback'; outcome: 'approved' | 'withheld' | 'rejected' | 'recorded'; reason?: string; recorded: number; entryIds: string[]; author: string; commentsError?: string }

parameters.name: mdPath
parameters.purpose: The artifact's .md under docs/, resolved and guarded exactly as workflow.artifactContent does.

parameters.name: comments
parameters.purpose: The new comments, in order. file is the repo-relative path of the document commented on (the .md, or an .html companion of this artifact) and defaults to the .md; version is the contentVersion the reviewer saw; anchor is present for an inline comment.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: The repository; falls back to the daemon's repo.

returns.meaning: The daemon validates the request, resolves the author once, then acts in a fixed order: the decision first, the comments second. approve calls the existing approveWorkflowTarget for this one artifact (and the existing follow-on for an approved bugfix issue, as 'workflow.approve' does); outcome is 'approved', or 'withheld' with the skip reason when the review gate holds it back. reject calls the existing rejectArtifactByJsonPath with the reason: the first whole-document comment if there is one, else 'Rejected in the review pane by <author>'; outcome is 'rejected'. feedback changes no state; outcome is 'recorded'. Then every comment is appended in one appendFeedbackBatch call with kind 'comment', the author, one batchId, and decision set to what happened: 'approve' or 'reject' when that took effect, 'feedback' for a feedback send and for an approval that was withheld. If the append fails after the decision took effect, the result still reports the outcome and carries commentsError, with recorded 0.

errors.condition: repo or mdPath missing or failing the docs/ guard; an unknown decision; a comment that is blank, longer than 10,000 characters, or whose file is neither the .md nor a companion listed in the artifact's body; more than 200 comments; feedback with no comments; the artifact not being a pending one for approve or reject; or the approve or reject call throwing. In each of these nothing is written.

preconditions: approve and reject need a pending artifact (no approvedAt, no rejectedAt); feedback is accepted in any state
postconditions: A comment is never saved with a decision that did not take effect
A decision with no comments writes no feedback entry
The existing IPCs workflow.pending, workflow.artifactContent, workflow.approve, workflow.resolveComment and artifact.feedback.append keep their shapes and behaviour
The author is decided by the daemon, never by the caller

parameters.name: idOrPath

parameters.name: comments
parameters.purpose: The drafts and the whole-document comment.

api.name: createDocsReviewHost
api.signature: createDocsReviewHost(deps: DocsReviewHostDeps): DocsReviewHost  // DocsReviewHostDeps gains: notifyChat?: (text: string) => 'sent' | 'queued' | 'unavailable'; companionUri?: (relPath: string) => string | undefined; frameSource?: () => string. DocsReviewHost is unchanged (open, dispose, openArtifact).

parameters.name: deps.notifyChat
parameters.purpose: Hands a decision message to the chat. Absent means no chat message is sent.

parameters.name: deps.companionUri
parameters.purpose: The webview address of an HTML companion under the repo's docs/ folder, or undefined when it may not be shown.

parameters.name: deps.frameSource
parameters.purpose: The webview's own resource origin, for the frame-src directive of the shell's CSP.

returns.meaning: LAYOUT. The shell is a column the height of the pane: a header (a select of pending documents, the open document's kind and state, and one tab per document of the artifact: the markdown first, then each HTML companion by title), a scroll region that holds the document, a collapsed strip of comments on the whole document, and the comment panel. Only the scroll region scrolls. THEME. Every colour, font and border comes from --vscode-* variables. The --it-* tokens the body, functional-requirement, diagram and experience renderers already use are defined for this surface from --vscode-* variables, so those renderers are not rewritten; renderTerminalStyle is no longer used by this pane and there is no theme message or switch. VIEWERS. A markdown document is rendered as today (marked, the section chooser, the functional, diagram and experience slots). An HTML companion is shown in an iframe whose src is deps.companionUri(relPath) and whose sandbox attribute is 'allow-scripts' only; when companionUri is absent or returns undefined the tab shows the file's path and a line saying it cannot be shown here. COMMENTS. On a markdown document, selecting text inside one block shows a round comment button; pressing it wraps the selection in a mark and opens a thread card under that block with a field and round add and close buttons. An added comment is a draft: dashed underline, tagged 'draft, not sent', removable. Its anchor is { quote, sectionSlug, prefix, suffix }: the selected text, the slug of the nearest heading above it from the section index, and up to 40 characters of the block's text on each side. Saved entries with an anchor are placed by finding the quote in the current document (first in the anchor's section with the prefix and suffix, then in that section, then anywhere when it occurs once; the document's own Feedback section is never searched); a placed passage gets a mark and a margin marker with the count, and clicking either opens its thread, oldest first, each with author, time and decision. An entry whose quote is not found, and every entry without an anchor, is listed in the whole-document strip, oldest first; one whose target.version differs from the view's contentVersion is tagged 'on an earlier revision' and shows its quote. Comments on an HTML companion are whole-document comments with that file as target. Drafts and the whole-document field are kept per artifact in the webview's saved state, so hiding and showing the pane does not lose them. DECISION. The three buttons post one 'docs-decision' { artifactId, decision, comments } with every draft and the whole-document comment; send feedback with no comment is refused in the webview with a line of text. The host calls client.decide once, posts 'docs-decision-result' { artifactId, ok, outcome, recorded, message }, and on success re-reads the pending list and the document. The webview clears its drafts only on ok with no commentsError. A read-only open (not awaiting review) shows the history and offers send feedback only. CHAT. After a successful decide the host builds one message and calls deps.notifyChat: the decision and outcome, the artifact id, title and docPath, the reviewer, and the new comments numbered in order, each with its quote and section when it has them; with no comments the message is the decision line alone. The result line in the pane says whether the chat message was sent, is waiting for the running turn, or could not be sent.

errors.condition: A failing decide, content or pending call is logged and shown as a line in the pane; drafts are kept. A failing or absent notifyChat never undoes a saved decision.

preconditions: The channel's panel was created with scripts enabled and, for HTML companions, with the repo's docs/ folder among its local resource roots
postconditions: The comment panel is visible at every scroll position of the document
No colour in the shell is a literal or a terminal token value
Nothing from an artifact reaches the DOM as markup except through the guarded markdown path that exists today; comments, authors and quotes are set as text
The pane holds no saved state of its own besides unsent drafts
The 'docs-list' and 'open-doc' messages and openArtifact behave as today

api.name: createChatPanelHost
api.signature: createChatPanelHost(deps: ChatPanelHostDeps): ChatPanelHost  // ChatPanelHost gains: submitExternal(text: string): 'sent' | 'queued' | 'unavailable'

parameters.name: text
parameters.purpose: A message to submit in the chat's current session as if the user had typed it.

returns.meaning: 'unavailable' when no agentic CLI is installed or the text is blank. Otherwise the chat panel is opened if it is closed (as open() does). If no turn of this host is running or waiting, the message is run at once through the same path a typed message takes (queued approvals are superseded, the user row is echoed and saved) and the answer is 'sent'. If a turn is running, the message is put on a first-in first-out list and the answer is 'queued'; when that turn reaches its end, errors or is stopped, the next waiting message is run, in the session that is active then. The list lives in memory only and is dropped when the panel is disposed.

dataModelChanges.details: Three optional fields. anchor?: FeedbackAnchor = { quote: string (the selected text, at most 500 characters); sectionSlug?: string; prefix?: string; suffix?: string (at most 40 characters each) } marks an inline comment. decision?: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'feedback' is the decision the entry was saved with. batchId?: string is shared by the entries of one decision. The existing target.file holds the repo-relative path of the document commented on and the existing target.version holds the contentVersion the reviewer saw. Entries written before this change have none of the new fields and stay valid. The JSON schema in provenance/schema.ts and coerceRequest in provenance/tool.ts accept the new fields.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: FeedbackEntry { id; author; timestamp; target { file; version?; segment? }; comment; kind?; + anchor?: { quote; sectionSlug?; prefix?; suffix? }; + decision?: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'feedback'; + batchId?: string }

dataModelChanges.details: docPath, contentVersion, feedback?, reviewer and state are added; every existing field is unchanged. DocsContent in the plugin mirrors them by indexing the daemon type, as it does for the structured records.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: ArtifactReviewView { artifactId; kind; renderedMarkdown; openQuestions; approvable; blockReason?; functionalDefinition?; erDefinition?; sequenceDefinition?; uxDefinition?; companions?; + docPath: string; + contentVersion: string; + feedback?: readonly FeedbackEntry[]; + reviewer: { name; source }; + state: 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected' }

dataModelChanges.entity: Webview protocol of the review pane (vscode-plugin/src/chat/protocol.ts)
dataModelChanges.details: 'docs-decision' changes from { artifactId, accept, note? } to { artifactId, decision: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'feedback', comments: { comment; file?; version?; anchor? }[] }. 'docs-content' gains docPath, contentVersion, feedback, reviewer, state and documents: { title; type: 'markdown' | 'html'; relPath?; uri? }[]. A new host message 'docs-decision-result' { artifactId, ok, outcome?, recorded?, message } is added to the kind list. The 'theme' message is no longer posted to this pane. migration.stateBefore: The review pane lays out its list, document, note box and buttons in page flow, in the chat's terminal style, so the controls come after the whole document (analyze bundle 4). Approve calls workflow.approve; request changes calls workflow.resolveComment with an empty anchor, which turns the note into a resolved open question, and is offered only for DEF, HLD and LLD (bundles 1 and 4). The artifact JSON has a feedback list with author, time, target and comment, appended one entry at a time through artifact.feedback.append; the review view does not return it, nothing carries it into a re-authored artifact, and a reject exists only as a function the CLI calls (bundles 2 and 3). The chat host can be given a message only by its own webview, and a new message supersedes a running turn (bundle 4).
migration.stateAfter: The pane is a column with a fixed comment panel under one scrolling document, in VS Code theme variables, with one tab per document of the artifact (the markdown and each HTML companion in a sandboxed frame). A reviewer drafts inline and whole-document comments and sends them with approve, reject or send feedback through one daemon call, workflow.reviewDecision, which records the decision and then appends the comments to body.feedback with the author the daemon resolves, an anchor for inline comments, and the decision that took effect. The review view returns the feedback list, a content version, the reviewer and the state; the pane shows saved comments on their passages or in a strip, oldest first. Re-authoring an artifact carries its feedback forward. After a decision the pane hands the chat host a message through submitExternal, which waits for a running turn. The older IPCs and the feedback entries already saved are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional anchor, decision and batchId fields to the feedback entry's type, schema, request coercion and renderer, and add the batch append and the prior-feedback helper
Carry the stored feedback into the new body in the five design finalizers
Add docPath, contentVersion, feedback, reviewer and state to the review view and export the user lookup
Add the review decision core and register the 'workflow.reviewDecision' handler
Add submitExternal and its waiting list to the chat host
Replace approve and comment in the plugin's review client with decide, change the 'docs-decision' message, add 'docs-decision-result', and move the host to the one call and the chat message

Rebuild the pane's shell: the column layout, the theme variables, the document tabs and frame, the comment panel, inline comments and the history; wire notifyChat, companionUri and the panel's local resource root in extension.ts
Update the daemon (push, update, restart) before installing the plugin build, then install the plugin and check by hand

migration.backwardCompat: Every change to a shape other clients read is additive and optional: the three new fields of a feedback entry, the five new fields of the review view, and one new IPC method. workflow.pending, workflow.artifactContent, workflow.approve, workflow.resolveComment and artifact.feedback.append keep their requests, responses and behaviour, so the JetBrains plugin, the CLI and the MCP tools are unaffected. Feedback entries already saved stay valid and render as before. Comments saved from the pane's earlier request-changes button remain where they were written, as resolved open questions; they are not converted. The plugin's webview protocol changes inside one plugin build. A plugin newer than its daemon gets an unknown-method error on a decision and shows it without saving anything, so the daemon is updated first. Rolling back the plugin or the daemon leaves the saved entries in place; an older reader ignores the fields it does not know.

alternativesConsidered.name: One review-decision call in the daemon over the existing feedback record
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A new IPC takes the decision and all new comments together; the daemon stamps the author, appends them to body.feedback and then approves or rejects.
alternativesConsidered.approach: FeedbackEntry gains three optional fields: anchor { quote, sectionSlug?, blockText? } for an inline comment, decision ('approve' | 'reject' | 'feedback') and batchId, and the existing target.version is filled with a content hash of the document the comment was made on. A new IPC workflow.reviewDecision { repo, mdPath, decision, comments[] } resolves the artifact as workflow.artifactContent does, resolves the author in the daemon (git user.name, else OS login), appends every comment in one write through a new appendFeedbackBatch in provenance/writer.ts, and only then calls the existing approve or reject function; it answers { decision, recorded, entries, approved?, skipped?, rejectedAt? }. The review view (ArtifactReviewView) gains feedback, contentVersion and reviewer. A second new IPC workflow.companionContent reads one HTML companion of an artifact under docs/. In the plugin the pane sends one docs-decision message with the drafts, the host calls the one IPC, re-reads the view, and hands a text summary to an injected notifyChat seam that extension.ts wires to a new chat host method which queues the message behind a running turn. workflow.resolveComment and artifact.feedback.append stay unchanged for their current callers.
pros: Comments and the decision are saved by one daemon call, in a fixed order, so a failed save never leaves an approval without its comments
The author is stamped by the daemon from the repo, the same for every client
Reuses the feedback record, its writer, the approve and reject functions and the user lookup
Existing IPC shapes are untouched, so the JetBrains plugin and the CLI are unaffected
The saved entries show in each document's Feedback section through the existing renderers
cons: Two new IPC methods to keep in step with the IDE fork's mirrored types
The record's type, schema and renderer all need the new optional fields

alternativesConsidered.name: The plugin composes existing calls
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The pane's host calls artifact.feedback.append once per comment, then workflow.approve or a thin new workflow.reject, and resolves the author itself.
alternativesConsidered.approach: FeedbackEntry gains the same optional anchor and decision fields, accepted by the existing artifact.feedback.append. The plugin's host resolves the author by running git config user.name in the workspace (else the OS user), appends each comment with one IPC call each, and then calls workflow.approve or a new workflow.reject that wraps rejectArtifactByJsonPath. The review view gains feedback so the pane can show history. The chat message is sent as in a1.
pros: The append call already exists and is tested
cons: Not one unit: a failure after some comments are saved leaves a partial batch, and a failure of the decision leaves comments with a decision that did not happen
Each append rewrites the whole artifact JSON, so ten comments are ten read-modify-write cycles
The author is decided by the client, so two clients can stamp different names for the same user
The plugin needs its own git lookup, duplicating the daemon's
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheaper, but it is partial on the two requirements that concern what is saved.

alternativesConsidered.name: A separate comments file per artifact
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Review comments go to a new sidecar file beside the artifact JSON, with their own read and write calls.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new file .insrc/artifacts/COMMENTS-<artifactId>.json holds review threads: each thread an anchor and a list of comments with author, time and decision. New IPCs workflow.comments.list and workflow.comments.submit read and write it; the decision is recorded as in a1. body.feedback is left as it is for the notes agents write.
pros: A shape made for threads, free of the feedback record's existing fields
The artifact JSON is not rewritten when a comment is added
cons: A second store beside the one that already records author, time and comment on an artifact
Review comments would not appear in the document's Feedback section without a second renderer
New files to commit, locate and keep with their artifact when it is moved or re-authored
More new code and tests than extending the record
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Works but ignores the record that exists and costs the most.

openQuestions: Can a VS Code webview show a repository HTML file that carries its own scripts (the diagram companions are about 3 MB with inline scripts) inside a frame with sandbox 'allow-scripts', addressed through the webview's resource address? This was not run. Recommended: try it first in the build; if it does not work, show the file's path with a control that opens it in the system browser.

Should comments saved by the pane's earlier request-changes button, which are stored as resolved open questions, be shown in the new history? Recommended: no; they stay in the document's resolved questions.
